moments.title: George Pullman builds a company town
moments.text: Between 1880 and 1884, the Pullman Palace Car Company built a model town for its workers beside its factory south of the city, with brick row houses, shops and churches the company owned.

moments.title: The Hotel Florence opens
moments.text: The company's hotel, named for Pullman's daughter, opened to house visitors and business guests.

moments.title: The Pullman Strike begins
moments.text: After the company cut wages without lowering rents, workers walked out. Eugene V. Debs's American Railway Union then refused to handle Pullman cars, and the boycott spread across the nation's railroads.

moments.title: Federal troops break the strike
moments.text: President Grover Cleveland sent U.S. Army troops and thousands of U.S. Marshals, and a federal injunction jailed the union's leaders, ending the strike.

moments.title: Arson at the clock tower
moments.text: An arsonist badly damaged the factory's Administration and Clock Tower Building. The state stabilized it, and the tower and clock were rebuilt by late 2005.

moments.title: A national monument
moments.text: President Barack Obama proclaimed Pullman a National Monument, the first National Park Service site in Chicago. Congress made it a National Historical Park in Dec 2022.

moments.title: Today: Pullman National Historical Park
moments.text: The restored clock tower building is the park's visitor center, opened Labor Day weekend 2021, and many of the original row houses are still homes.
